te: Report on the Internal Security Act followed up, and a framework for studying border security set
se: Agenda: Progress in preparing the report on the study of the Internal Security Act B.E. 2551 (2008) (the Senate has not yet published the summary of this meeting, so this text is the agenda in the meeting notice, not a resolution of the meeting)
it: Progress in preparing the report on the study of the Internal Security Act B.E. 2551 (2008)
Framework for preparing a study report on security along Thailand's borders with neighbouring countries

te: Study visit to the southern border prepared, and a working group set up to study the Internal Security Act
se: The meeting asked for the work plan for fiscal year 2026 to be revised in line with the observations before it is presented at the committee's seminar on 4 December 2025. It approved questions on complaints about problems in the southern border provinces for the trip to receive information in Betong District, Yala Province, and Sirindhorn Camp, Yarang District, Pattani Province, on 26–29 November 2025, and set up a 10-member working group headed by a Vice-Chair of the subcommittee to prepare the report on the study of the Internal Security Act B.E. 2551 (2008)
it: Work plan for fiscal year 2026 for the committee's seminar
Questions on complaints about problems in the southern border provinces, for the trip to receive information, 26–29 November 2025
Report on the study of the Internal Security Act B.E. 2551 (2008)

te: Agencies heard on the use of security laws, and a work plan in 5 areas set
se: The meeting invited representatives of the Office of the National Security Council, the Internal Security Operations Command and the Ministry of Interior to give information on problems in enforcing security laws and on duties and powers under the Internal Security Act B.E. 2551 (2008). It gave the agencies observations so that the law can be enforced more effectively, and will gather the information to prepare a report for the Senate. It also approved preparing a work plan and strategy on security in 5 areas for the committee
it: Problems in enforcing security laws, and duties and powers under the Internal Security Act B.E. 2551 (2008)
The subcommittee's work framework

te: Work framework for fiscal year 2026 set, and hearings with security agencies prepared
se: Agenda: Consideration of the subcommittee's work framework for fiscal year 2026 (meetings, study visits, seminars and spending framework) (the Senate has not yet published the summary of this meeting, so this text is the agenda in the meeting notice, not a resolution of the meeting)
it: Consideration of the subcommittee's work framework for fiscal year 2026 (meetings, study visits, seminars and spending framework)
Consideration of inviting the Office of the National Security Council, ISOC and the Ministry of Interior to give information for the report

Consideration of joining the committee's meeting on 29 October 2025 on a complaint about the overlapping area along the Thai–Myanmar border, Cho Po Ro Subdistrict, Kra Buri District, Ranong Province (referred by the committee)

te: Information from the study visit to ISOC summarised, and explanations on Ko Kut
se: The meeting exchanged views from its study visit to ISOC on 21 August 2025 on enforcing security laws to respond to fast-changing threats, and approved sending letters requesting information and inviting ISOC, the NSC and the Ministry of Interior to a meeting. It then discussed the explanations given by representatives of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Department of Mineral Fuels on enforcing the law on territory, sovereignty, natural resources and national interests concerning the area of overlapping continental shelf claims between Thailand and Cambodia in the sea around Ko Kut
it: Information from the study visit to ISOC on enforcing security laws
Explanations by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Department of Mineral Fuels concerning the area of overlapping continental shelf claims between Thailand and Cambodia in the sea around Ko Kut

te: Questions for the ISOC study visit prepared, and agencies heard on Ko Kut
se: The meeting approved questions for the study visit to ISOC on 21 August 2025 and considered questions on the area of overlapping continental shelf claims between Thailand and Cambodia in the sea around Ko Kut, inviting representatives of the Department of Mineral Fuels, Ministry of Energy, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to attend. It approved joining the committee's meeting on this matter
it: Questions for the study visit to ISOC
Questions on the area of overlapping continental shelf claims between Thailand and Cambodia in the sea around Ko Kut

te: ISOC study visit set, Ko Kut report reviewed, and a study on building national resilience begun
se: The meeting approved a study visit to ISOC on 13 August 2025 and inviting representatives of the Office of the National Security Council and the Ministry of Interior for the study of improving the Internal Security Act B.E. 2551 (2008). It approved inviting representatives of the Ministry of Energy, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Department of Mineral Fuels and Trat Province to give information in line with the committee's observations on the draft report on Ko Kut, and approved in principle a strategic study report on "Building National Resilience to Maintain State Security Sustainably"
it: Improving and amending the Internal Security Act B.E. 2551 (2008)
Draft report on the study of the area of overlapping continental shelf claims between Thailand and Cambodia in the sea around Ko Kut (in line with the committee's observations)
Strategic study report: building national resilience

te: Assigned to review the Thai-MECC budget for 2026, and a study visit on security laws prepared
se: The meeting noted that the ad hoc committee considering the draft Annual Appropriations Act for fiscal year 2026 had asked the Committee on Military Affairs and State Security to send representatives to consider security budgets on 31 July 2025. The subcommittee was assigned to consider the budget of the Thai Maritime Enforcement Command Center (Thai-MECC) and assigned representatives to attend. It also approved a study visit to gather information on improving the Internal Security Act B.E. 2551 (2008)
it: Joint consideration of the 2026 security budget (Thai-MECC part) with the ad hoc committee
Plan for gathering information to improve and amend the Internal Security Act B.E. 2551 (2008)

te: Request for a study visit to ISOC to study security laws approved
se: The meeting considered a plan for gathering information to study improvements to laws and regulations that are problems or obstacles to maintaining national security, and approved seeking approval for a study visit to the Internal Security Operations Command
it: Study of improvements to laws and regulations that are obstacles to maintaining national security

te: Approach set for studying improvements to the Internal Security Act
se: The meeting considered the approach and plan for gathering information to study improvements to the Internal Security Act B.E. 2551 (2008), approved draft questions, and assigned the responsible subcommittee member to explain the details at the next meeting
it: Approach and plan for gathering information to improve and amend the Internal Security Act B.E. 2551 (2008)

te: Study report on Ko Kut approved for submission to the committee
se: The meeting approved the report on the study of the area of overlapping continental shelf claims between Thailand and Cambodia in the sea around Ko Kut for submission to the Committee on Military Affairs and State Security, and noted the joint meeting with the committee that day on building a security road through forest areas in Mae Hong Son Province, at which representatives of the Royal Thai Army, the 3rd Army Area, the Naresuan Task Force, the Singhanat Task Force and the Armed Forces Development Command gave information
it: Report on the study of the area of overlapping continental shelf claims between Thailand and Cambodia in the sea around Ko Kut
Building a security road through forest areas, Mae Hong Son Province (joint meeting with the committee)

te: Questions on the eastern border and Ko Kut prepared, and more advisers appointed
se: The meeting noted that the Chair of the committee had assigned the Chair of the subcommittee to visit the Chong Hin Mu operating base, Rap Ro Subdistrict, Tha Sae District, Chumphon Province, to learn about problems along the Thai–Myanmar border. It then approved questions to agencies on relations and security on the eastern border, Thai–Cambodian border crossings, maritime claims, and the issuing of land title documents on Ko Kut, and approved proposing the appointment of additional advisers
it: Visit to the Chong Hin Mu operating base, Chumphon Province, as assigned by the Chair of the committee
Questions on the eastern border, Thai–Cambodian border crossings and Ko Kut
Appointment of additional advisers to the subcommittee

se: The meeting noted a letter from Na Pho Phatthana Subdistrict Municipality inviting a visit to hear views on disasters and water management, which the Chair of the subcommittee will attend in person, approved the summary of the study visits to Ranong and Chumphon, and approved holding a workshop on 17–21 March 2025, as local administrative organisations had asked for consideration of an area-based security project
it: Letter of invitation from Na Pho Phatthana Subdistrict Municipality on disasters and water management
Summary of the study visits to Ranong and Chumphon Provinces
Workshop on area-based security, 17–21 March 2025

te: Chumphon–Ranong study visit summarised, and agencies contacted on riverbanks and malaria
se: The meeting noted a letter from a civil society network in the southern border provinces asking about progress on the budget for accident prevention in the area, and the outcome of the committee's meeting on 21 January 2025 on the complaint about boundary marker 73. It then discussed information from the study visits to Chumphon and Ranong on 24–26 January 2025, asking for a letter requesting support from the Department of Local Administration to build the remaining sections of riverbank, and for coordination with the Department of Disease Control on the malaria outbreak in Tha Sae Subdistrict
it: Letter from a civil society network on the accident prevention budget in the southern border provinces
Outcome of the committee's meeting on the complaint about boundary marker 73
Information from the study visits to Chumphon and Ranong Provinces

te: Joint meeting with the committee: readiness of state agencies in the event of war
se: The subcommittee met jointly with the Committee on Military Affairs and State Security to ask about the readiness of government agencies should war make it impossible for people to live normally, including food, energy, communications and public order. Representatives of the Office of the National Security Council, ISOC and the agencies concerned explained their roles and contingency plans under the law
it: Readiness of state agencies to provide basic necessities in the event of war
